title: Mamatoya Website
subtitle: Commercial Restaurant Website
summary: Commercial restaurant website focused on branding, SEO, and responsive design.

overview.title: Overview
paragraphs: Mamatoya is a commercial restaurant website that translates brand and content requirements into a responsive public web experience.
The implementation prioritizes clear presentation, mobile usability, foundational search visibility, and maintainable delivery within the project's commercial constraints.

responsibilities.title: Responsibilities
items: Translate business and branding requirements into Vue page structures.
Implement responsive layouts for desktop and mobile visitors.
Arrange imagery and content sections to support the restaurant's visual presentation.
Apply foundational page metadata and SEO considerations.
Deploy and maintain the public website with Firebase Hosting.
Balance visual requirements, delivery cost, and future content maintenance.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: The website is implemented as a Vue frontend and delivered as a responsive static web experience through Firebase Hosting.
highlights: Reusable Vue page sections organize brand and restaurant content.
Responsive CSS adapts the content hierarchy across screen sizes.
Static assets and page metadata support presentation and discoverability.
Firebase Hosting provides the public delivery layer.

items.title: Translating brand direction
items.description: Commercial content and visual goals must be converted into an implementation that remains clear, responsive, and maintainable.

items.title: Mobile presentation
items.description: Image-heavy brand content requires deliberate sizing, ordering, and spacing to preserve usability on smaller screens.

items.title: Delivery trade-offs
items.description: Implementation choices balance design expectations, development effort, hosting simplicity, and later content adjustments.

deployment.title: Deployment and Operations
paragraphs: The production site is delivered through Firebase Hosting with a deployment flow suited to a frontend-focused commercial website.
highlights: Build and verify the responsive frontend before release.
Publish the generated site through Firebase Hosting.
Maintain content and layout behavior as commercial requirements evolve.

lessons_learned.title: Lessons Learned
items: Commercial frontend work requires balancing brand expression with practical usability.
Responsive behavior should be considered while structuring content, not added only after desktop completion.
Simple deployment and maintainable page structure support efficient follow-up changes.
